title: Employment & Work Injury
intro: Employment and work injury in India: wages, leave, retrenchment, occupational safety and statutory benefits.

tips.title: Overtime in India: the OSH Code sets an 8-hour day and a 48-hour week
tips.cost: No direct cost. Keep attendance records, shift rosters and written overtime approvals.
tips.inPlainWords: The four labour codes commenced on 21 November 2025. The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 sets the general daily limit at 8 hours and the weekly limit at 48 hours (section 25(1)(a)). Overtime and its rate are governed by the Code on Wages, 2019 and the applicable state rules; where the Code applies, overtime is payable at twice the ordinary rate. Check your establishment, role and state rules, and keep attendance records.
tips.benefit: The OSH Code fixes an 8-hour day and a 48-hour week at section 25(1)(a). The Code on Wages, 2019 (section 14) provides overtime at twice the ordinary rate where it applies. The Factories Act, 1948 is repealed, so do not rely on its 9-hour day or its overtime provisions.
tips.sources: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (section 25). <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Code on Wages, 2019 (section 14). <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Ministry of Labour and Employment commencement notifications, 21 November 2025. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Coverage and exemptions depend on the establishment and state. Managerial and supervisory staff may be outside the working-hours provisions. State rules may add conditions.

tips.title: Annual leave under the OSH Code: one day for every 20 days worked
tips.cost: No cost. Keep leave records and your appointment letter.
tips.inPlainWords: The OSH Code, 2020 (section 32) gives one day of annual leave with wages for every 20 days worked. At the 180-day qualifying threshold that is 9 days; a worker who works about 300 days can reach 15. The Factories Act 1948 and its 240-day threshold are repealed. Encashment is on demand under the Code, not an automatic 300% payment.
tips.benefit: OSH Code section 32: one day per 20 days worked, with a 180-day qualifying threshold and 9 days at that threshold. The old Factories Act section 79 is repealed. State Shops Acts may provide different leave.
tips.sources: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (section 32). <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; State Shops and Establishments Acts; Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The 180-day threshold and carry-forward rules are in the Code and state rules. Do not use the old 240-day or 12-day calculation.

tips.title: There is no fixed national probation ladder in India — read the contract and state rules
tips.cost: No cost. Read the offer letter and the applicable state Shops rules before signing.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not set a general one, two or six month probation limit by contract length. Probation is a contractual term, and the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and state Shops rules may govern confirmation and termination. Probation pay cannot fall below the applicable minimum wage, but the 80% rule is not Indian law. Check the appointment letter for the probation length, notice, confirmation test and extension clause.
tips.benefit: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and state Shops Acts set procedures for covered establishments. A probation clause that is unfair or vague may be challenged, but there is no statutory maximum for every job.
tips.sources: Industrial Relations Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Code on Wages, 2019. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; State Shops and Establishments Acts.
tips.caveats: Coverage depends on the establishment and state. Do not accept a second probation after confirmation without written advice. Keep the letter and any extension.

tips.title: Retrenchment compensation under the Industrial Relations Code: 15 days average pay per completed year
tips.cost: No cost. Use your last 12 months wages and service record.
tips.inPlainWords: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 is repealed. Retrenchment is now governed by the Industrial Relations Code, 2020. Section 70(b) keeps 15 days average pay for each completed year of continuous service, with notice or pay in lieu under section 70(a). Gratuity is separate: the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 is repealed and the benefit continues under the Code on Social Security, 2020 (section 53), after five years.
tips.benefit: Industrial Relations Code section 70(b): 15 days average pay per completed year. Code on Social Security section 53: gratuity after five years at 15 days wages per year. The old Industrial Disputes Act and Gratuity Act are repealed.
tips.sources: Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (section 70). <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Code on Social Security, 2020 (section 53). <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; commencement notifications, 21 November 2025.
tips.caveats: Not every employee is a workman; managerial staff may rely on contract. Retrenchment procedure and thresholds depend on establishment size and state.

tips.title: Notice pay under the Industrial Relations Code — there is no automatic N+1
tips.cost: No cost. Read the notice clause and keep the termination letter.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no universal N+1. The notice period is usually in the appointment letter or standing orders. For retrenchment, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 section 70(a) requires notice or pay in lieu. State Shops Acts and the Code set different procedures. Check what your contract says, and get any waiver or payment in lieu in writing.
tips.benefit: Industrial Relations Code section 70(a); state Shops Acts. Payment in lieu may be contractual or statutory, not a universal one-month add-on.
tips.sources: Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (section 70). <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; State Shops and Establishments Acts.
tips.caveats: Contracts can be challenged if the notice clause is unfair, but litigation takes time. Do not sign a full and final settlement before checking dues.

tips.title: Challenge a wrongful termination under the Industrial Relations Code — there is no fixed 2N
tips.cost: Time and legal fees; free legal aid may be available through NALSA.
tips.inPlainWords: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 is repealed. A workman can raise an industrial dispute under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020; the labour court or industrial tribunal may order reinstatement, back wages or compensation. Managerial employees may need a civil suit or arbitration under the contract. Limitation and forum depend on the Code and state. Get legal advice before accepting a settlement.
tips.benefit: Industrial Relations Code, 2020 remedies and NALSA legal aid. Remedies are fact-specific and can include reinstatement or compensation, not a fixed multiplier.
tips.sources: Industrial Relations Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; NALSA legal aid. <https://nalsa.gov.in/legal-aid/>
tips.caveats: Delay can bar a claim. The employer may argue misconduct or redundancy. Preserve the termination letter, emails and performance records.

tips.title: Do not sign a resignation you do not mean — check gratuity and EPF under the Codes
tips.cost: No cost; keep copies of everything you sign.
tips.inPlainWords: Resignation is usually governed by the contract and state Shops rules. The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 is repealed; gratuity continues under the Code on Social Security, 2020 (section 53) after five years. EPF remains under the EPF Act, 1952. A resignation can affect notice and final settlement, but statutory gratuity and EPF should not be forfeited. Ask for the calculation in writing.
tips.benefit: Code on Social Security section 53; EPF Act, 1952; state Shops Acts.
tips.sources: Code on Social Security, 2020 (section 53). <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; State Shops and Establishments Acts.
tips.caveats: Some employers make settlement conditional on a resignation letter. Get advice before signing if dues are disputed.

tips.title: Save your employment records before you hand back the laptop
tips.cost: About half an hour; no cost.
tips.inPlainWords: Before you leave, save your appointment letter, pay slips, attendance, leave records, PF and ESIC statements and written communications. You will need them to prove wages, notice and contributions. Do not take source code, client lists or confidential documents; that can create a separate dispute.
tips.benefit: Good records make an EPFO or ESIC complaint or a labour claim possible. The employer may restrict access after exit.
tips.sources: Author experience; EPFO employee portal. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Keep only your own employment records. Do not copy trade secrets or client data.

tips.title: Before a dusty, noisy or chemical job, ask for the hazard disclosure and medical checks
tips.cost: No cost; ask before you sign.
tips.inPlainWords: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 requires employers to identify hazards, provide protective equipment and arrange medical examinations in covered establishments. The exact exams and frequency depend on the process and state rules. Ask for the hazard information in writing and keep your medical reports.
tips.benefit: The OSH Code and state factory rules require hazard controls and medical checks in many hazardous processes.
tips.sources: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; State factory rules.
tips.caveats: Coverage varies by establishment and process. A generic medical check is not enough; ask what is tested and who pays.

tips.title: Dust, noise and chemicals can cause permanent damage — use the right protection and report unsafe work
tips.cost: Employer-provided equipment; keep your own records.
tips.inPlainWords: Silicosis, noise-induced hearing loss and chemical injuries can be permanent. The OSH Code, 2020 requires employers to provide effective protective equipment and safe systems of work. Workers can report unsafe conditions to the inspector. Keep records; if you face retaliation, get legal advice — the remedy depends on the facts and the provision invoked.
tips.benefit: The OSH Code and ESIC cover prevention and occupational disease. Prevention is the only reliable protection for many conditions.
tips.sources: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not rely on a general statement that retaliation is illegal; the remedy depends on the facts. Report symptoms early. A respirator needs fit testing to work.

tips.title: Report a workplace injury at once and start the ESIC or Social Security Code claim
tips.cost: No cost; keep medical records and witness details.
tips.inPlainWords: Report the injury immediately and get medical treatment. If covered by ESIC, the employer should help with the accident report and claim. The Employees Compensation Act, 1923 is repealed; employee compensation now sits in Chapter VII of the Code on Social Security, 2020. Do not assume a commute is covered: employment injury generally requires an accident arising out of and in the course of employment. Get advice on the facts.
tips.benefit: ESIC and Chapter VII of the Code on Social Security, 2020. Treatment, cash compensation and dependants benefits may be available in covered cases.
tips.sources: ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Code on Social Security, 2020, Chapter VII. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>
tips.caveats: Commuting injuries are generally outside ESIC unless the facts bring them into the course of employment. Contractor and principal-employer liability can be complex.

tips.title: If you feel acutely unwell at work, call 112 first — do not delay for a compensation theory
tips.cost: No cost.
tips.inPlainWords: There is no rule requiring you to wait 48 hours or stay at work to qualify for compensation. If you have chest pain, stroke signs, severe bleeding or breathing trouble, call 112 and get emergency help. Ambulance numbers vary by state; ask the 112 operator or the local hospital. Report the episode and keep records; any ESIC or Code claim can follow.
tips.benefit: 112 is the Emergency Response Support System number. Emergency care comes first; ESIC and the Code on Social Security may apply later.
tips.sources: Ministry of Home Affairs, Emergency Response Support System. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not drive yourself. Ambulance access varies by state; confirm the local number.

tips.title: An uninsured employer is still liable for a work injury
tips.cost: Time and legal help; free legal aid may be available.
tips.inPlainWords: If the employer did not insure you under ESIC, the claim does not disappear. Employee compensation now sits in Chapter VII of the Code on Social Security, 2020, and principal employers can be liable for contractor workers under the OSH Code. Keep proof of employment, wages and the accident. A no-insurance, no-compensation statement is not a legal defence.
tips.benefit: Code on Social Security, Chapter VII; ESIC; OSH Code Chapter IX. The employer may have to pay from its own funds.
tips.sources: Code on Social Security, 2020, Chapter VII. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, Chapter IX.
tips.caveats: Proving employment and the accident is the key. Contractor chains can be complex.

tips.title: Disability assessment follows ESIC and the Social Security Code; check the schedule
tips.cost: Time; no direct fee for the statutory process.
tips.inPlainWords: After a work injury stabilises, ESIC or the Code on Social Security, 2020 provides for medical assessment and disability benefit. The Code and its schedules set the percentage and compensation; specified injuries can have fixed percentages, so do not assume a purely discretionary figure. Do not sign a one-time settlement before the assessment; get the report and the calculation.
tips.benefit: ESIC and Chapter VII of the Code on Social Security, 2020, including its schedules.
tips.sources: ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Code on Social Security, 2020, Chapter VII and schedules. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>
tips.caveats: Appeals and second opinions may be possible. A private doctors estimate is not the statutory assessment.

tips.title: Work-related death benefits come from ESIC and the Social Security Code
tips.cost: Administrative time; legal aid may be free.
tips.inPlainWords: If a worker dies from a work injury, dependants may claim ESIC benefits or compensation under Chapter VII of the Code on Social Security, 2020. The amount depends on wages, the scheme and the dependants. EPF and gratuity may also be payable. Report the death, keep the medical and employment records, and get help from a union or legal-aid lawyer.
tips.benefit: ESIC; Code on Social Security, Chapter VII; EPF; gratuity under section 53.
tips.sources: ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Code on Social Security, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Dependants must prove relationship and dependency. Time limits apply.

tips.title: Document workplace bullying and use the POSH or internal grievance route where it applies
tips.cost: Time; legal help may be needed.
tips.inPlainWords: Sexual harassment at work is covered by the POSH Act, 2013, which requires an internal committee in covered workplaces. General bullying or verbal abuse may be misconduct under the contract or the Industrial Relations Code, but India has no single anti-bullying statute for all workplaces. Record dates, witnesses and messages; use the internal committee, HR or the labour authority. Retaliation can strengthen the case.
tips.benefit: POSH Act, the Industrial Relations Code and cohort research on workplace bullying and health. The health risk is real, but the legal route depends on the conduct.
tips.sources: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013. <https://wcd.gov.in/>; Kivimaki M et al. (2003). Workplace bullying and the risk of cardiovascular disease and depression. Occupational and Environmental Medicine 60(10):779-783. <https://doi.org/10.1136/oem.60.10.779>
tips.caveats: POSH covers sexual harassment, not every form of bullying. Do not wait if your safety is at risk.

tips.title: Ask for a relieving letter and service certificate when you leave
tips.cost: No cost.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian statutes do not give every employee a single 15-day file-transfer right, but your contract, standing orders or state Shops rules may require an experience or relieving letter. Ask in writing before your last day and keep a copy. PF and ESIC records are separate and should be updated.
tips.benefit: State Shops Acts, standing orders and EPFO/ESIC records support the exit. A service certificate helps the next employer.
tips.sources: State Shops and Establishments Acts; EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no universal statutory form. If the employer refuses, a written request and labour complaint may help.

tips.title: Check the income-tax treatment of your severance before you spend it
tips.cost: A chartered accountant fee, or free portal guidance.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not exempt severance up to three times the average wage. Retrenchment compensation has a limited exemption under section 10(10B) of the Income Tax Act, subject to the prescribed limit; gratuity, leave encashment and VRS have separate rules. Relief under section 89 may apply. Ask a chartered accountant or use the income-tax portal before assuming the whole amount is tax-free.
tips.benefit: The Income Tax Act sections 10(10B), 10(10C), 10(10AA) and 89, and the Income Tax Department portal, set the treatment.
tips.sources: Income Tax Department. <https://www.incometax.gov.in/>; Income Tax Act, 1961.
tips.caveats: Limits and conditions change. Do not rely on an employers withholding as final.

tips.title: Keep your EPF and ESIC records portable when you change states
tips.cost: No cost; online transfer.
tips.inPlainWords: Your EPF account follows you through your UAN; transfer it when you change jobs instead of withdrawing. ESIC records are linked to your insured person number and can be used across states. Update your nominee and keep your passbook and contribution history. There is no household-registration barrier to these transfers.
tips.benefit: EPFO and ESIC portability keeps your contribution history continuous and helps at retirement and at a claim.
tips.sources: EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Employer compliance varies. Check your passbook after each job change.

tips.title: Get a written offer letter and employment contract — India has no double-wage penalty for a missing one
tips.cost: No cost.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian law does not impose the double-wages-after-one-month rule for a missing written contract. But a written appointment letter is still essential to prove wages, notice, probation and duties. The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and state Shops and Establishments Acts require written terms and records in covered establishments. If the employer refuses to give a contract, keep emails, payslips and attendance.
tips.benefit: The Contract Act, the Industrial Relations Code and state Shops Acts make written terms important. Written terms reduce disputes.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Industrial Relations Code, 2020; State Shops and Establishments Acts.
tips.caveats: Oral contracts can be enforceable but are harder to prove. Do not refuse to sign a contract you have accepted without advice.

tips.title: If EPF or ESIC contributions are missing, complain to EPFO or ESIC and keep your wage records
tips.cost: No cost; time.
tips.inPlainWords: Check your EPF passbook and ESIC contribution history. If contributions are missing or underpaid, raise a grievance with EPFO or ESIC and keep payslips, bank statements and appointment letters. A resignation over the employers statutory breach may affect your notice and dues, so get advice before you resign. A voluntary waiver of PF or ESIC is not a lawful substitute for contributions.
tips.benefit: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (EPF and ESIC provisions) and the EPFO/ESIC grievance portals provide the route.
tips.sources: EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Code on Social Security, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Contractor and principal-employer responsibility can be shared. Time limits apply.

tips.title: Penalty clauses on resignation are enforceable only to a reasonable extent in India
tips.cost: Legal advice.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian courts do not enforce every penalty clause. Under section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a court may award reasonable compensation for breach, not the full penalty. A training bond or notice-period recovery may be enforceable if it is reasonable and reflects actual loss. Post-employment non-compete clauses are often hard to enforce. Get the clause reviewed before you pay.
tips.benefit: The Indian Contract Act section 74 and case law require the court to look at reasonableness and actual loss.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872 (section 74). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: No fixed formula. A clause that is a penalty, not a genuine pre-estimate, may be reduced.

tips.title: Object in writing to a demotion or salary cut — do not wait and hope it reverses
tips.cost: No cost; legal help may be needed.
tips.inPlainWords: A unilateral demotion or salary cut can be a breach of your contract or standing orders. Write to the employer immediately, state that you do not accept the change, and keep working under protest if you need the income. Indian law has no one-month rule that automatically makes the change valid, but continuing without objection can weaken your case. Get legal advice.
tips.benefit: The Contract Act, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and state Shops Acts support a prompt written objection and preserve the dispute.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Industrial Relations Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; State Shops and Establishments Acts.
tips.caveats: The outcome depends on the contract and the employers power to transfer or redeploy. Do not resign without advice.

tips.title: Contract workers: check the OSH Code threshold and the principal employer
tips.cost: No cost.
tips.inPlainWords: The Contract Labour Act, 1970 is repealed. Contract labour is now regulated by the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020; the Code threshold for principal-employer obligations is 50 contract workers (section 45). Principal employers can be liable for wages and welfare when the contractor fails, and EPF and ESIC may also apply. Keep your attendance, wage and contractor details.
tips.benefit: OSH Code Chapter IX and section 45; EPF and ESIC. Principal-employer liability is the key protection.
tips.sources: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (section 45). <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Coverage thresholds and state rules vary. Equal pay for equal work is not automatic in every contract-labour case.
